claims: Effective April 20, 2026, the United States Army raised its maximum enlistment age to 42 years old.
The updated policy applies to the Regular Army, Army National Guard, and Army Reserve.
Individuals can enlist up to and including age 42, with or without prior military service.
As of April 2026, the minimum enlistment age is 17 years old with parental consent or 18 years old without parental consent.
As of April 2026, the maximum enlistment age is 42 years old.
The maximum age was previously 34 or 35, depending on the specific component.
The new policy is outlined in the updated Army Regulation 601-210.
Applicants with prior service may qualify if their age minus prior honorable active service is less than 43.
Recruits must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident with a valid Green Card.
The Army removed the waiver requirement for individuals with a single prior conviction for marijuana possession or paraphernalia.
The Air Force maximum enlistment age is 42.
The Space Force maximum enlistment age is 42.
The Coast Guard maximum enlistment age is 42.
The Navy accepts recruits up to 41.
The Marine Corps maintains a limit of 28.
